restated: For all integers q >= r >= 0, f(q,r) <= q + r + 1. Consequently, for each fixed r the quantity f(q,r) - q is at most r + 1 for every q >= r.
ledger_statement: For all q >= r >= 0, f(q,r) <= q + r + 1. Proof: induction over the three branches of the recurrence. In the mex branch the set {f(a,r):a<q} u {f(q,b):b<r} has at most q+r elements, so among the q+r+1 positive integers 1..q+r+1 one is missing and the mex is at most q+r+1; the r>q branch gives f(q,q) <= 2q+1 <= q+r+1; the stale branch gives f(q-1,r) <= q+r. Corollary: max_q (f(q,r)-q) <= r+1, which discharges (Z1) of byrnes_audit.md with C=1.

verdicts.gap_description: The proof is a valid lexicographic induction. Branch (A) applies the induction hypothesis at (q,q) <_lex (q,r); branch (B) follows directly from the branch condition f(q-1,r) < q; branch (C) uses only the cardinality bound |S| <= q+r and the pigeonhole fact mex(S) <= |S|+1 <= q+r+1, which equals q+min(q,r)+1 because branch (C) is reached only when r <= q. No step fails.

Tight set (f = q+r+1) on q,r<=1000 is exactly row r=0 plus (1,1), matching the submission's claim.

verdicts.effectivity_check: Effective and computable. The bound constant is produced explicitly by the line 'The least positive integer outside S is therefore at most q + r + 1: f(q,r) = mex(S) <= q + r + 1', following |S| <= q+r. No appeal to eventual periodicity or any existence-only quantity is made. Note: this bound controls the VALUES f(q,r)-q <= r+1 and does not itself bound the preperiod N(r); the submission states this limitation explicitly, and the corollary is only offered as one input (a computable C = 2 with max_q(f(q,r)-q) <= C*r) to a separate argument.

verdicts.gap_description: No gap found. The proof is a valid induction over the lexicographic order on (q,r): branch (A) applies the induction hypothesis at (q,q) with q<r; branch (B) uses the branch condition f(q-1,r)<q directly; and in branch (C), since S = {f(a,r): a<q} ∪ {f(q,b): b<r} has at most q+r elements, at least one of the q+r+1 integers 1,...,q+r+1 is outside S, so mex(S) ≤ q+r+1. Branch (C) is only reached when r≤q, giving exactly q+min(q,r)+1.
